question: As of March 14, 2024, which of the following is the world’s tallest statue?
solution:
The correct answer is __**Statue of Unity, Gujarat**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• The Statue of Unity, located in Gujarat, India, is the world's tallest statue, standing at a height of 182 meters (597 feet).
 
• It was unveiled on October 31, 2018, in honor of Sardar Vallabhbhai Patel, the first Deputy Prime Minister and Home Minister of India.
 
• The statue is situated on the banks of the Narmada River near the Sardar Sarovar Dam in Kevadia.
 
• Designed by Indian sculptor Ram V. Sutar, the statue is made of bronze-clad reinforced concrete.
 
• The project was completed at a cost of approximately ₹2,989 crore and aims to promote tourism and educate visitors about Sardar Patel's contributions to India's unity.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Other Tall Statues in India:**

 
 
• Tathagata Tsal in Sikkim: A statue of Lord Buddha standing at 41 meters.
 
• Thiruvalluvar Statue in Kanyakumari: Dedicated to Tamil poet Thiruvalluvar, standing at 40.6 meters.
 
• Adiyogi Shiva Statue in Coimbatore: A 34-meter tall statue of Lord Shiva promoting yoga and spirituality.
 
 
 
• **Global Tall Statues:** The Spring Temple Buddha in China was previously the tallest statue in the world at 128 meters before being surpassed by the Statue of Unity.
 
• **Engineering Marvel:** The Statue of Unity is designed to withstand wind speeds of up to 180 km/h and earthquakes measuring up to 6.5 on the Richter scale.
 
• **Tourism Impact:** The Statue of Unity has become a major tourist attraction, drawing millions of visitors annually and boosting the local economy.
 
• **Cultural Significance:** Sardar Patel is remembered as the "Iron Man of India" for his role in unifying the country post-independence, making the statue a symbol of national integration.
